quantity: MACL 2025 arrivals as % of Yearbook intl arrivals
mechanism: MACL is a per-flight extract covering only part of the year's flights; it is not a census
verdict: FLAG: usable for shape, not for level

quantity: MACL turboprop arrivals as % of Yearbook domestic arrivals
mechanism: No domestic region exists in the extract; its 88 turboprop flights are the only comparable movement, against 3,987 domestic arrivals per day. Domestic is seaplane and Dash-8, tracked elsewhere
verdict: FAIL: MACL cannot describe domestic traffic

quantity: MACL adult arrivals as % of Yearbook intl arrivals
mechanism: Restricting to adults removes children and infants, which the Yearbook includes
verdict: INFO: the 36.5% previously quoted is this adult-only figure

quantity: correlation of MACL monthly volume with Yearbook monthly intl arrivals
mechanism: MACL holds a near-constant 533 flights every month (CV 0.013), so it carries no seasonal signal
verdict: FAIL: do not use MACL for seasonality

quantity: Avas airport dropoffs as % of Yearbook intl departures per day
mechanism: Taxi is one mode of several; the remainder is ferry, bus and private car
verdict: PLAUSIBLE: a 10-25% taxi mode share is credible

quantity: Avas airport pickups as % of Yearbook intl arrivals per day
mechanism: Arriving passengers mostly use pre-booked transfers, resort boats and the RTL bus, so recorded taxi pickups are far fewer than dropoffs
verdict: FLAG: pickups and dropoffs are not symmetric; never assume they are

mechanism: Counts aeroplanes, ignoring how full they are. An 80-seat turboprop and a 300-seat widebody count the same
verdict: INFO: this weighting understates the morning peak

mechanism: Counts people, which is what bus demand depends on. The morning widebody bank is full, so it carries more of the total than its flight count suggests
verdict: PASS: this is the defensible figure for demand, and it supports ~33-35%

quantity: share of 2025 arrivals in 07:00-09:00, widebody passenger-weighted
mechanism: Long-haul arrivals only; the sub-population with the least alternative to a taxi
verdict: INFO: upper bound on the morning concentration

mechanism: Window ends at 13:00. On this weighting the peak is midday, which is the artefact that makes the morning claim look wrong
verdict: INFO: do not use flight weighting for demand

mechanism: Window ends at 09:00, i.e. the morning peak is real once passengers rather than flights are counted
verdict: PASS: confirms the F4 tri-peak claim
